_vantages_comment: Arbitrary-length list of capture points. Adding a 3rd vantage (e.g. a PE-side tap) means appending one entry here plus one entry to 'visibility' below -- no code should special-case a count of exactly 2.
_visibility_comment: Per vantage: 'direct_peers' are nodes whose point-to-point sessions (BGP TCP session, BFD, OSPF adjacency) terminate at this vantage -- only these nodes' LOCAL protocol-state changes (BFD down, OSPF neighbor loss, TCP RST) are directly observable here. 'reflects_routes_from' lists other vantages whose PE-originated BGP EVPN routes are still visible at this vantage via RR-to-RR route reflection (RFC 4456) -- i.e. BGP UPDATE/WITHDRAWAL content is visible network-wide through the RR mesh even though local link/session-state events are not. This split is what makes the RR-Down vantage-flip case fall out generically: RR2 has RR1 in its own direct_peers, so RR2 directly observes RR1's session drop as a local event -- no fault-type-specific branch needed to know RR2 can report on RR1's failure.
_ground_truth_comment: Per-PE expected values, confirmed live via vtysh against the running fabric on 2026-07-31 (not copied from pcap2story's topology.yaml, which only has route_target and no RD/ESI fields at all). expected_rd follows FRR's live-confirmed auto-derivation pattern <bgp_router_id>:<instance>, instance=2 observed uniformly across all 5 PEs for VNI 100. esi is set only for PE1/PE2, which share an EVPN multihoming ESI on their vhost100 attachment (confirmed via 'show running-config': es-id 12, es-sys-mac 02:00:00:00:12:12, type-3 ESI 03:02:00:00:00:12:12:00:00:0c). PE3/PE4/PE5 have plain non-ES vhost100 interfaces and no ESI.
